correctness.rationale: Every finite B_n is explicitly defined with absorbing constant zero and relational multiplication. Four rank<=3 sentences distinguish the boundaries n=1,2,3,4; each is true exactly for n at most its index via the endpoint-idempotent coverage characterization, with nonzero guards preventing an absorbing-zero counterexample. For all m,n>=5, the three-round EF strategy copies all endpoint equality patterns in the first two rounds. At the last round an otherwise unrepresentable six-distinct-index triple has pairwise-annihilating nonzero elements and can be represented with only five indices by using a repeated row coordinate, preserving all equality and ternary multiplication atoms. This proves the infinite classification. Two independently structured exact finite-type recursions and a sentence evaluator pass their recorded tests; finite enumeration is not used to infer the tail.

value.rationale: A complete sharp quantifier-depth classification of the standard finite matrix-unit Brandt family is a natural logical invariant of inverse semigroups. Three element selections involve up to six matrix indices, but a structurally invisible repeated row allows stabilization already at five. Explicit index-cover sentences prove each of four lower boundaries is necessary. The exact five-class classification has self-contained interest independent of more general theorems and is not a cosmetic reparametrization or arbitrarily restricted enumeration.
